findings.note: The default-fail verification contract is not passing: required regression and placeholder-scan checks are explicitly false, and the contract also states its spec_revision predates the amended specification. T-001 therefore lacks valid quality-gate evidence for the current implementation.

The independent security PASS covered a deleted predecessor artifact with no recorded digest. The document explicitly says the shipped runner has substantive post-review changes and still requires a fresh independent security review, so T-001's security-review Done-When condition is unmet.

The Windows handle-relative publishing, rename, and reparse-point path has never been executed; both reported green entrypoints exercised the PowerShell suite on macOS and therefore the Unix publisher. This leaves a material cross-platform gap for a high-risk runner intended to modify protected files on Windows.

A failure in the batch-wide Test-PostCopyHashes phase occurs after Copy-Payload has completed, leaving FailedTarget null. The live-state report then enumerates installed files but no FAILED target, despite the design requiring post-copy-phase failures to identify the failed target; current TEST-012 covers only a mid-copy failure.
